title: Baby Bonfire
description: An open exploration of small home objects that bring fire, water, air, earth, light, weather and sound indoors without a screen. Concept sketches only.
notice: Nothing has been manufactured or tested.
Do not burn anything indoors on the strength of these pages.

idea.pieces: The objects. Anything with a tag can be a piece.
idea.places: Small tiles or marked spots around a home. A place notices which piece has landed by a tag on the piece, plus heat and light. Never cameras or microphones.
idea.flame: A lit flame is a condition met, and the room responds.
idea.roaming: Pieces move around the house, and carrying them is part of the ritual.
idea.linkedPlaces: One home's light can show in another.

scenes.name: Light the Hearth
scenes.summary: Stack three pallets, carry a flame over from the candle, and put the lid on when you are done.

scenes.name: The Shelf
scenes.summary: Five stone places and seven pieces. Set the shelf, light the hearth, and see what the room does.

scenes.name: The Roaming Shelf
scenes.summary: A home seen from above. Carry eight pieces between seventeen places and the arrangement is the message: a piece on the entry shelf says home, three on the table start dinner.

scenes.name: The Rounds
scenes.summary: Carry a piece to a spot in the house at dawn, midday, dusk or night. The house answers.

scenes.name: The Helper
scenes.summary: A teapot-size helper on three wheels does small chores around an evening home: it carries stray pieces back to their tiles, brings the snuffer and waters the fern. A dial sets how much it does on its own, and it never lights a flame.

scenes.name: Any Object, Any World
scenes.summary: Stick a dot on anything you love and it becomes a piece. Then change the whole room around it.

scenes.name: The Home Press
scenes.summary: Five small machines on one bench: clay, wax, paper, felt and food. Design a piece, watch it made, and read what a home machine would still need. Sources as read Nov 11, 2026.

scenes.name: Paired Hearths
scenes.summary: Two rooms in two homes. Light one hearth and the other one glows.

scenes.name: Mesh Street
scenes.summary: Light a hearth and watch the signal cross a small town by near hops, rooftop radios and internet relays. Embers wait when a path is missing.

scenes.name: House Power
scenes.summary: Tap a cutaway house to gather tiny amounts of energy from sun, heat, water, footsteps and a hand crank into one ember bank, then spend it on small signs of presence. Every sum is shown, with sources as read Nov 11, 2026.

scenes.name: Stations
scenes.summary: Four places that like company: a drum, a voice, a dance floor and a stretch by the window.

scenes.name: The Table
scenes.summary: A table seen from above with six seats, one of them kept for someone far away. Three pieces begin a meal; light the covered flame for dinner, pass the plate, hold a pause, then wash up. Three table worlds: wood, tile and a metal one on Mars.

scenes.name: Weather in the House
scenes.summary: Six pieces that follow the sky outside: fog, wind, swell, rain, sun and moon. Simulated here.

scenes.name: Creatures
scenes.summary: One house, one yard, one day. Set out seed, water, a blanket, a bell, a ball and a stone, move the time from dawn to night, and see which animals come to which place.

scenes.name: Four Seasons
scenes.summary: Turn a year wheel and one home changes with it: where the noon light lands, which pieces come out of the bin, the scent logs, the sound bed and one gathering for each season.

scenes.name: Five Levels of Magic
scenes.summary: The same hearth at five levels, from a flame that reacts to a shelf that knows the date and the tide.

scenes.name: Seven Homes
scenes.summary: One idea in seven houses, where each element gets a built place in the wall. Then build your own.

scenes.name: The Cabinet of No Bounds
scenes.summary: Sixteen home objects nobody can make yet. Each does one thing, wants a gesture and has a cost.

scenes.name: Ritual Atlas
scenes.summary: Thirty-five things people do with fire, water, air, earth, light and sound when something in life changes.

scenes.name: Anchors and Open Time
scenes.summary: A house that keeps a few fixed moments on three rings and leaves everything else alone.

scenes.name: Precedents Wall
scenes.summary: Other people's work in the directions this exploration is heading, each described in our words with a link out.

workshop.name: Open spec v0
workshop.summary: The place, the piece, four signals, the rules, fire safety rules and what is undecided.

workshop.name: Open mesh notes
workshop.summary: How places could talk inside a home and between homes. Opt-in per object, no account. No network exists.

workshop.name: Barter board
workshop.summary: Makers trading parts of the system. No payments, no prices.

workshop.name: Make a piece
workshop.summary: How to contribute a scene, a piece idea, a printer or laser file, a test result or a ritual.

kits.name: First place
kits.summary: A printable place: a tile with a landing ring, a tag recess and a puck bay, a blank puck, and an optional untested sensing puck shell with a vented lid. It holds no flame.
notice: Nobody has printed or built this yet.
This place holds no flame. Keep printed plastic away from candles, stoves and anything hot.
Not a product. Nothing is for sale. No health claims.

screens.name: Prayer Fire
screens.summary: A film of a small fireplace, with sound. Light it, say what it is for, give the words to the flame and sit for about a minute. Press and hold to blow on it.
screens.why_a_screen: Baby Bonfire is about objects without a screen. This page stands in for a hearth nobody has made yet. It is the one page here that plays a film and recorded sound, and it lights no real flame.
screens.sound: Starts only when the Light the fire button is pressed. One button turns it off.

media.what: A twelve-second looping film of the fireplace, with no sound track.
media.made: A generated picture animated with a Seedance video model through Krea, then joined forward and backward into a loop.

media.what: The first frame of the film.
The same fireplace before it is lit.
media.made: The first frame with the flame edited out using the Krea 3 image model.

media.what: A quiet music bed, 75 seconds, looped.

screens.words: By Claude. None of them are Mike Hoydich's.
screens.tested: A scripted run in headless Chrome at phone and desktop sizes on 2026-11-11. Not yet heard by a person or run on a phone.

screens.name: The Room
screens.summary: A small alcove with the fireplace lit on a table, to look around on a phone or a laptop or to stand in with a WebXR headset. Press and hold the fire to blow on it. Three doors lead to Prayer Fire, On Your Table and the town in 3D.
screens.why_a_screen: Baby Bonfire is about objects without a screen. This room is a picture of one such object at its real size, 13 cm tall, for looking at before anything is made. It lights no real flame.
screens.sound: Starts only when the Sound button is pressed.

media.what: The fireplace as a 3D model, 13 cm tall, 24,988 triangles, 447 KB.
media.made: Generated from a picture with Tencent Hunyuan3D 3.1 through Krea, then simplified, scaled and compressed.

media.what: A plain stand-in used only if the detailed model fails to load.
media.made: Built from simple shapes in code.

media.what: The same fire crackle as Prayer Fire.

screens.tested: Headless Chrome and an emulated Quest 3 on 2026-11-11. Not yet tried in a headset or on a phone.

screens.name: On Your Table
screens.summary: The fireplace as a 3D model to turn and zoom. Where a phone or headset supports AR, it can stand on a real table at its real size, 13 cm tall.
screens.why_a_screen: A way to see the size of the object in a room before anyone makes one. It is a picture of an idea, not a design to build from.

media.what: The same model with no compression, 941 KB, so a phone's own AR viewer can read it.
media.made: Generated from a picture with Tencent Hunyuan3D 3.1 through Krea, then simplified and scaled.

media.what: A plain stand-in used only if the detailed model fails to load.
media.made: Built from simple shapes in code.

media.what: A still of the model shown while it loads.
Google's model-viewer 4.4.0, the element that shows the model and opens AR.
media.made: Vendored, Apache-2.0, licence file beside it.

screens.tested: The model loads in headless Chrome on 2026-11-11. AR itself has not been tried on any device.

screens.name: A Higher Purpose
screens.summary: A small island of square tiles at dusk, in 3D, with a hearth at the centre and places for water (a pier), air (four posts and floating cubes) and ground (standing stones). A loop is made as it plays at 88 beats a minute; each place brings its own layer forward when near.
screens.why_a_screen: It is a place to stand in rather than an object, drawn small and scaled up square in sixteen colours.
screens.sound: Made in the browser with the Web Audio API; no audio files. Starts only on the Begin tap; one button turns it off; it stops when the tab is hidden.
screens.devices: Phone (drag to look, tap to walk, optional tilt), desktop (drag, WASD or arrows) and headsets that offer immersive VR (look at a place for a moment, or point and select).
screens.words: By Claude. None of them are Mike Hoydich's.
screens.tested: A scripted run in headless Chrome at phone and desktop sizes on 2026-11-11. Not yet run on a real phone or in a headset.

privacy: No account. Lit windows on the hub are kept in the visitor's browser (localStorage key bb-street-v1) and sent nowhere. Prayer Fire keeps one number in the visitor's browser, the count of finished sits (localStorage key bb-prayer-v1); the words typed there are never stored or sent. A Higher Purpose stores nothing and sends nothing. The Room and On Your Table keep nothing. On Your Table sends nothing itself, but if AR is started on Android, Google's Scene Viewer opens and is given the model's address on this site to fetch it. The pages make no outside requests; Prayer Fire loads its film and sound from its own folder, and the three 3D pages (The Room, On Your Table and the town at /vr/) load their models and their code (three.js and model-viewer, both vendored) from this site.
credits: Sketches made with Claude at Mike Hoydich's direction, 2026-11-11.
